concepts.def: A short, memorable musical idea that can be developed.
A musical sentence, often 4 bars long.

walkthroughs.h2: The seed of every great piece
walkthroughs.body_html:
A motif is a tiny idea — often just 2–5 notes — that you can grow throughout your piece. Beethoven's Symphony No. 5 famously uses a four-note motif (short-short-short-long).

Try writing a 4-note motif on a single rhythm. Then repeat it, transpose it, change one note — these techniques are development.

Most melodies move in 4-bar phrases, often paired as 'question and answer'. The first phrase ends with an open-sounding imperfect cadence; the second phrase ends with a closed-sounding perfect cadence.

Use a sequence (motif moved up or down) to keep ideas familiar but fresh.

Binary form (AB) has two contrasting sections — perfect for short dances. Ternary form (ABA) brings back A after a contrasting B, giving a satisfying 'return home'.

Choose a clear structure before composing — it stops your piece from wandering and helps the listener follow.
